HIV infection leads to fibrosis and loss of lymphatic tissue T cells, and that this fibrosis limits T-cell repopulating capacity even after highly active antiretoviral therapy is initiated.
collagen deposition in lymphoid tissue contributes to the depletion of CD4 + T-cells in HIV-1 infection and limits immune recovery in HIV-1-infected and SIV-infected individuals.
collagen deposition in lymphoid tissue contributes to HIV-1 and simian immunodeficiency viruses (SIV) pathogenesis by limiting the expansion and differentiation of CD4+ cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that collagen deposition and fibrosis play in the pathogenesis of HIV-1 infection.
the role of collagen deposition in the pathogenesis of HIV-1 and simian immunodeficiency viruses and the implications for immune reconstruction.
the role of collagen in the development of fibrosis in HIV-infected lymph nodes.

collagen deposition and fibrosis are important contributors to the loss of CD4+ cells during HIV-1 infection.
the role of collagen deposition and fibrotic damage in lymphoid tissue is a significant contributing factor in CD4+ T cell decline in HIV-1/SIV infections.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fibrotic process in the lymphatic tissues is not a direct result of HIV-1 or SIV infection but is rather a consequence of the host immune response to the infection.
the lymphoid tissues of HIV-infected individuals are not only the primary site of HIV replication, they are also the site where the virus causes the most profound and irreversible immune damage.
the lymphatic tissue fibrosis is a consequence of HIV-1 infection, which in turn contributes to CD4 T-cell depletion and limits CD4 T-cell repopulating during HAART.
The main takeaway from our work is that
collagen accumulation in the lymphatic tissue microenvironment is an important determinant of the CD4+ T cell decline and immune reconstitution that occurs during HIV-1/sIV infections.
the lymphoid tissue microenvironment is a critical determinant of CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell homeostasis.
collagen deposition in lymphoid tissue, as a result of HIV-1 infection and/or immune reconstitution, can lead to a loss of T-cell function and a decrease in T-cell number.
